findings.problem: Every screen change rebuilds main by clearing innerHTML, which destroys the focused button. Focus falls to BODY on every single transition, so a keyboard or voice user re-tabs from the top of the document at every step of a seven-step game. Measured after entering a scene and after advancing to Choice 1: document.activeElement is BODY both times.
findings.fix: After each go(), move focus to the new screen's heading (see OUTLINE-BROKEN) with tabindex=-1 and .focus({preventScroll:true}). One line in go(), and it fixes the whole game at once.

findings.problem: The page authors no focus style at all. It inherits the UA ring, measured as outline 1px rgb(16,16,16) on a lobby button - a 1px near-black hairline against near-black ink borders. On a founder-profile build that is not a visible ring, and nothing in the comfort ladder or the DARK HOST LAW fork governs it.
findings.fix: Author :focus-visible with a 3px outline in --amber plus a 2px offset, declared once for button and applied at every comfort stop so the ring is measured like everything else.
findings.evidence: stylesheet scan for :focus selectors returned NONE; computed outline 1px rgb(16,16,16)

findings.problem: No screen carries a heading. The only h1 is the persistent site title in the header, so assistive tech is handed an empty outline exactly where the player is standing. The per-screen title (SCENE 1 OF 3, CHOICE 1 OF 3, YOUR STAGING) is styled as a paragraph.
findings.fix: Promote .stepline to <h2> on every screen. Purely semantic - the CSS already carries the look.
findings.evidence: querySelectorAll('main h1,h2,h3,[role=heading]') returned NONE on a choice screen
